h1: The 7 Best Lawn Mowers Under $1000 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $1000: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best lawn mowers under $1000 in 2026, covering cordless, gas, corded and reel mowers for every yard size.
summary: The EGO LM2134SP-2 is the best mower here for medium and larger lawns: a 21 inch deck, self-propelled drive and a cordless platform with no fuel. The Greenworks 80V delivers the same format for less. Flat standard lawns are well served by the EGO LM2114 push model, while the PowerSmart suits anyone committed to gas. Small yards can drop to the Greenworks 40V, reel or corded picks.
intro: Nobody shopping under $1000 for a mower should plan to spend $1000. Cut-off prices like that tempt people toward riding-class thinking, yet every machine in this ranking costs far less, and the gap between the cheapest and the dearest is mostly drive type and battery platform. Deck width and slope decide whether a mower feels effortless or like a second job.

The classic error is buying engine or voltage bragging rights instead of cutting width. A 14 inch reel and a 21 inch self-propelled deck differ by about a third in strip width, which is a third more passes across the same grass. We ranked seven mowers, cordless, gas, corded and manual, by Primea's scoring from spec sheets and owner feedback, and rewarded the ones whose tradeoffs match real lawns rather than showroom comparisons.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Self-Propelled Mower LM2134SP-2
products.verdict: A full-size cordless mower with self-propelled drive on a broad battery platform.
products.description:
EGO's LM2134SP-2 is the mower to buy when the lawn is bigger than a postage stamp and you refuse to haul gas. It pairs a 21 inch deck with self-propelled drive on the company's cordless battery platform. That drive matters because it matches wheel speed to your walking pace, so the pushing effort that tires you on a slope or a long afternoon mostly disappears.

It ranks first because it is the only pick that combines full deck width, drive assist and zero fuel in the $500 and up tier. The Greenworks 80V matches that format for less, but EGO's platform is the more established of the two and shares batteries with other tools from the same maker.

Medium to large lawns, with any slope at all, reward it most. The caveat is cost and weight: it is the priciest cordless here and heavier than the push models, so skip it for a small flat yard.
products.idealFor: Medium to large lawns where drive assistance matters.
products.skipIf: You have a small flat yard.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Self-propel and a 21 inch deck without paying near the top price.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is the sensible answer if EGO's price makes you wince. It brings a 21 inch deck, self-propelled drive and an 80V 4Ah battery with a charger in the box, all in the $200 to $500 tier. That puts drive assist at roughly the cost of a basic push mower, which is why it earns the value label.

It sits second rather than first because of the battery. Four amp hours is a modest reserve for a 21 inch cutter, and the platform is the less flexible of the two, with fewer companion tools and a thinner accessory range than EGO's.

Buy it for a medium lawn where you want drive assist without paying top money. Skip it for a very large property, since a single 4Ah pack will run out before a big yard is finished and a spare is an extra purchase.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting self-propel without top pricing.
products.skipIf: You have a very large lawn.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Push Mower
products.verdict: A full-width EGO deck without the self-propel premium.
products.description:
The EGO LM2114 answers a question many buyers get wrong: do I need drive assist at all? On a standard flat lawn, probably not. This is a 21 inch deck on the 56V battery platform, sold with battery and charger in the $200 to $500 tier, and it cuts the same swath as the self-propelled models above it.

It lands third because it hands the pushing back to you. Against the Greenworks 80V, which costs in the same tier and adds drive, the EGO trades convenience for a better-established battery system and a lighter feel without a drive motor.

Buy it for a level lawn of ordinary size. The caveat is slopes. Pushing a 21 inch deck uphill, with grass-clippings loading the deck, is where you will wish you had paid for the drive on the two models above.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has slopes or is large.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyGlide 21-Inch Gas Mower
products.verdict: Gas runtime without any battery to manage.
products.description:
PowerSmart's EasyGlide is the only gas mower in the group, and it makes the case for staying with an engine in plain terms. A 144cc 4-stroke OHV engine drives a 21 inch deck with 3-in-1 mulch, bag and side discharge, and it runs until the tank is empty. There is no battery to charge, no capacity to ration and no platform to buy into.

It ranks fourth because that freedom costs routine upkeep: fuel, oil changes and spark plug care, plus more noise than any cordless pick above it. The two EGO models and the Greenworks 80V remove all that for similar or higher spending.

Choose it if your lawn is large enough that battery runtime worries you, or you already keep fuel and tools for gas equipment. It is a poor fit for anyone who wants quiet, low-maintenance mowing, and it has no self-propel.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: A light, easy-to-store cordless mower for small yards.
products.description:
Greenworks' 40V push mower is the one to shop when storage space matters more than strip width. Its 16 inch deck runs off a 40V 4Ah battery with a charger, giving 160Wh of included energy, and it sits in the $200 to $500 tier. The smaller deck keeps weight down, so it hangs on a wall hook easily.

It ranks fifth because narrow decks cost time. Compared with the 21 inch EGO LM2114 at the same tier, you make about a quarter more passes across the same grass, and 160Wh does not stretch much further than a small yard.

This is the right buy for townhouse lawns and tight sheds. The honest caveat is that medium or large lawns turn into a slog, and if you have any area to cover, the full-width EGO and Greenworks 80V are better value for the work.
products.idealFor: Small lawns and tight storage spaces.
products.skipIf: You have a medium or large lawn.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: No motor, battery or fuel, just a manual reel for small flat lawns.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 removes every running cost: no motor, no battery, no fuel, just four reel blades turning as you walk. Its 14 inch width suits a small patch of level turf, and it costs in the $50 to $100 tier. Scissor-style reel cutting is also kinder to grass blades than a spinning rotary cut.

It ranks sixth because reel mowers only work under tight conditions. Against the corded LawnMaster below it, the reel is quieter and needs no outlet, but the LawnMaster at least powers through grass a little taller than a reel tolerates.

Buy it for a small, flat yard mowed often, where the quiet is part of the appeal. Skip it if the grass gets ahead of you between cuts. Tall or thick growth jams the reel and makes the 14 inch swath feel narrower still.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets tall between cuts.

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1114K 15-Inch Corded Mower
products.verdict: A cheap corded mower with no battery to replace.
products.description:
LawnMaster's MEB1114K is the budget corded option, and it suits a very specific yard. Its 11-amp motor spins a 15 inch deck from a wall outlet, so there is no battery to buy, charge or replace later, and it costs in the $100 to $200 tier. The motor is the same kind of simple, dependable design that corded tools have long used.

It ranks last because the cord is the constraint. The reel mower above it needs nothing but effort and can roam anywhere, while the LawnMaster must stay within cord reach and drag its tether around trees and beds.

Buy it for a small, open lawn near an outlet where simplicity and a low outlay matter. Skip it if the yard has obstacles or distance, since managing the cord around them is tiring and the narrow deck means extra passes.
products.idealFor: Small unobstructed yards near an outlet.
products.skipIf: Your yard has trees, beds or distance.

whatMatters.detail: Deck width is the cutting strip the blade covers on each pass. It matters concretely: moving from a 14 inch reel to a 21 inch deck cuts the number of passes by about a third on the same lawn. Estimate your lawn area before you shop, then check the stated deck width in the title or bullets, since manufacturers sometimes quote blade length instead.

Self-propelled drive powers the rear or front wheels so you steer rather than push. It matters on slopes, in thick grass and on lawns where the walk is long, and it adds cost and weight. Look for the words self-propelled in the title or spec bullets, and be wary of listings that only say easy push or smooth glide.

Battery voltage names the platform; amp hours set the runtime. A 4Ah pack feeding a 21 inch cutter runs a smaller yard per charge, while a bigger pack lasts longer. On the listing, find the stated Ah rating, check whether a battery and charger are included, and see whether a second pack is sold for the same platform.

Gas mowers need fuel, periodic oil changes and spark plug care, and they run until the tank empties. That unlimited runtime is the appeal, but the upkeep and noise are the price. Check the engine size and four-stroke or two-stroke designation on the listing, and decide honestly whether you will keep up with maintenance each season.

Corded and reel mowers solve cost, not terrain. A cord limits range and snags on beds and trees, while a reel mower stalls in tall or thick grass. Both suit small yards only. On the listing, check the cord rating or the blade count, and match it against how tall your grass actually gets between cuts.

cards.text: Quiet, no fuel and minimal upkeep, with runtime set by battery size. Picks here: the EGO LM2134SP-2, EGO LM2114, Greenworks 80V and Greenworks 40V.

cards.label: Gas

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to cordless unless the lawn is very large.

faq.q: Is $1000 too much for a lawn mower?
faq.a: Almost always, yes. Every mower in this ranking costs well below that figure, and even the EGO LM2134SP-2 sits in the $500 and up tier. Spend for deck width, drive type and battery platform that fit your lawn, not to use the whole budget.

faq.q: What is the biggest mower buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing deck width badly. A 14 inch reel like the American Lawn Mower 1204-14 on a large lawn means endless passes, while a 21 inch deck such as the EGO LM2114 finishes the same area much faster. Match width to the area you mow weekly.

faq.q: Is self-propelled worth it over a push mower?
faq.a: On slopes and larger lawns, yes: the EGO LM2134SP-2 and Greenworks 80V make a hilly yard far less tiring. On a small, flat plot, the EGO LM2114 push model gives the same 21 inch cut for less weight and money.

faq.q: How do I set up a cordless mower?
faq.a: Charge the battery fully, seat it in the mower and set the cutting height before the first cut. Greenworks 80V and EGO models include a battery and charger, so there is nothing else to buy. Fold the handle into position and read the safety latch instructions in the manual.

faq.q: How do I maintain a lawn mower?
faq.a: Clean the deck after each mow so clippings do not cake on, sharpen or replace blades every year and keep batteries on their correct charger. The PowerSmart gas mower also needs oil changes and spark plug care. Store every model dry and out of the weather.

faq.q: Can a reel mower handle my lawn?
faq.a: Only if the lawn is small, flat and cut often. The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 slices short grass quietly with no fuel, but tall or thick growth jams its four reel blades. Bigger or neglected lawns need a motorized deck like the LawnMaster or any cordless pick.

finalTake: Pick the EGO LM2134SP-2 if your lawn is medium or large and you want drive assist without fuel, or the Greenworks 80V for the same layout at a lower tier. A flat standard lawn is fine with the EGO LM2114. Choose the PowerSmart only if you want gas, and keep the reel, corded and 16 inch Greenworks for small yards where simplicity beats cutting width.
